_comment: Carte épisode → schéma et en-têtes de tableau. Choix ÉDITORIAL, donc hors du code : une figure doit éclairer le mécanisme de l'épisode, jamais le décorer. Un épisode sans figure pertinente n'en reçoit pas — mieux vaut rien qu'un schéma hors sujet. Les en-têtes sont propres à chaque série parce que « What to check / What it means » ne convient pas à un catalogue de contraintes techniques.

bonds-and-rates/episode-01.md.key_line: Two bonds showing 5.2% over eight years, one callable in two, are not the same instrument, and only yield to worst says so out loud.
bonds-and-rates/episode-01.md.takeaway: A quoted yield is a claim about a contract you have not read yet.

bonds-and-rates/episode-02.md.key_line: The working rule: percentage price change equals minus duration multiplied by the yield change.

chart.title: One bond, four market yields
chart.subtitle: Ten-year bond, $1,000 face, 4% coupon — price in dollars at each market yield.

data.note: Same contract, same coupon — only the market yield changes.

bonds-and-rates/episode-03.md.key_line: The spread on its own hides whether the market repriced the next twelve months, the next thirty years, or both at once.
bonds-and-rates/episode-03.md.takeaway: Without both maturities and both legs on the page, a curve label is a nickname, not a finding.

bonds-and-rates/episode-04.md.key_line: Treat a spread move as evidence that something was repriced, then go test the reason against filings and transaction data.

bonds-and-rates/episode-05.md.key_line: The right choice is the one whose residual risks you have identified, sized and agreed to monitor, not the one with the most convenient ticker.

bonds-and-rates/episode-06.md.key_line: Give the bond sleeve a job instead, and write the job on paper.
bonds-and-rates/episode-06.md.takeaway: A bond sleeve without a written job is a slogan, not a plan.

central-bank-playbook/episode-01.md.key_line: A mandate is the job a law hands the institution.
central-bank-playbook/episode-01.md.takeaway: Target, tool, event, interpretation — four fields, and only the last one is yours.

central-bank-playbook/episode-02.md.key_line: Judge the stance on that column, never on the headline.

chart.title: The real rate is the one that bites
chart.subtitle: Policy rate minus inflation, the same subtraction the episode performs in each case.

data.note: nominal rate minus inflation, as stated in the text

central-bank-playbook/episode-03.md.key_line: Announced pace and realised change are two different series.
central-bank-playbook/episode-03.md.takeaway: A pace is not a stock, and a cap is not a delivery.

numbered_titles.0: Before you write about a balance-sheet announcement

chart.title: Monthly runoff caps, in two parts
chart.subtitle: These are announced ceilings, not what actually ran off.

central-bank-playbook/episode-04.md.key_line: The change from the previous statement is the signal, so read the two side by side rather than reading the new one alone.
central-bank-playbook/episode-04.md.takeaway: Read each document for the job it does, in the order it arrived.

numbered_titles.0: How to work an FOMC day

central-bank-playbook/episode-05.md.key_line: It is a choice of series, and the choice changes the answer.
central-bank-playbook/episode-05.md.takeaway: Name the series before you argue about the number.

numbered_titles.0: How to work a macro release

central-bank-playbook/episode-06.md.key_line: Then treat the first market move as evidence, not as proof you were right.

correlation-and-seasonality/episode-01.m.key_line: It is a property of the window you chose.

numbered_titles.0: Housekeeping, before you trust the number

correlation-and-seasonality/episode-02.m.key_line: It was a hypothesis with a shelf life.
correlation-and-seasonality/episode-02.m.takeaway: When the sign flips, mark the rule inactive rather than inventing a story that saves it.

correlation-and-seasonality/episode-03.m.key_line: Small samples are why calendar effects look so convincing and behave so badly.

numbered_titles.0: Freeze the test before you look at the answer

correlation-and-seasonality/episode-04.m.key_line: Any average built from three paths is not a law.

correlation-and-seasonality/episode-05.m.key_line: If you cannot say what would make you close it, you do not have a strategy.

correlation-and-seasonality/episode-06.m.key_line: A number you cannot rebuild is not evidence.
correlation-and-seasonality/episode-06.m.takeaway: Rebuilding a number tells you where it came from. It never tells you the number is right.

economic-calendar/episode-01.md.key_line: It reacts to the gap between what arrived and what was expected, and to nothing else.

chart.title: Payrolls, March 2026: the level was expected, the gap was not
chart.subtitle: Previous month, forecast, actual — the forecast was already in the price.

data.note: the 232,000 miss is what the market had not priced

economic-calendar/episode-02.md.key_line: Averaging the two headlines into one word, strong or weak, throws away the actual information.

economic-calendar/episode-03.md.key_line: The monthly figure is where the real momentum lives.
economic-calendar/episode-03.md.takeaway: Read the layer before the label: the month before the year, the components before the headline, and two more releases before the conclusion.

economic-calendar/episode-04.md.key_line: Do not fuse the releases into one verdict because a verdict reads better.

economic-calendar/episode-05.md.key_line: Calling the language hawkish or dovish is interpretation, not the record.
economic-calendar/episode-05.md.takeaway: Record the action first, the explanation second, and never let the adjective outrank the vote.

economic-calendar/episode-06.md.key_line: If a gap straight through your stop would breach what you can afford to lose, the position is already too big for the event.

etf-toolkit/episode-01.md.key_line: Costs come in three parts and only one is advertised.
etf-toolkit/episode-01.md.takeaway: The ticker tells you which index. It cannot tell you what the wrapper charges, what it hides, or how much of it is one bet.

numbered_titles.0: Read the wrapper in this order

etf-toolkit/episode-02.md.key_line: In a real panic, rates, credit, currencies and equities move together, and the correlation you measured over a calm five years cannot prove a hedge will work during the next stress.

numbered_titles.0: Map the risk before the return

etf-toolkit/episode-03.md.key_line: The problem is inheriting it without choosing it.

numbered_titles.0: Open the holdings file in this order

chart.title: Drift is corrected by where new money goes, not by selling
chart.subtitle: The same account in three states. Nothing was sold between the second and the third.

etf-toolkit/episode-04.md.key_line: Automating the first does nothing for the second.

numbered_titles.0: Set the rules in this order

etf-toolkit/episode-05.md.key_line: Resetting the leverage every evening simply means day two's multiplier applies to a different base than day one's.

numbered_titles.0: Before the first trade, in this order

chart.title: The same two days, told twice
chart.subtitle: Same start, same shape of move, and a 1% index loss becomes a 9% fund loss.

etf-toolkit/episode-06.md.key_line: Choose the drawdown you can actually live with, not the headline return.

chart.title: Four templates, four different holes to sit through
chart.subtitle: Worst fall from a previous high, as this episode states each one.

gap-risk-survival/episode-01.md.key_line: Size an overnight position as though its stop may fill at the next available price, not at the trigger.
gap-risk-survival/episode-01.md.takeaway: A stop is an instruction to leave, not a promise about the price you leave at.

table_titles.0: Four questions before you hold overnight

gap-risk-survival/episode-02.md.key_line: Stress the instrument you own, not the chart you watch.
gap-risk-survival/episode-02.md.takeaway: Two expressions of one thesis can differ more than two theses.

gap-risk-survival/episode-03.md.key_line: Decide the stressed price before you decide the size.

chart.title: Same news, same stop, same open
chart.subtitle: Loss on a €50,000 account when the stock opens at €70 instead of stopping at €90

gap-risk-survival/episode-04.md.key_line: Each had a named reference price, a trigger, an invalidation taken from structure, and a clock.
gap-risk-survival/episode-04.md.takeaway: Trade the reason for the gap, never the size of it.

gap-risk-survival/episode-05.md.key_line: What separated the two groups was whether the cash, the network or the customers were still there the next morning — a question about evidence, not about a percentage on a screen.

high-beta-proxies/episode-01.md.key_line: It is a measurement of the past, not a promise about tomorrow.

high-beta-proxies/episode-02.md.key_line: Buy it because you expect the index to rise and you have not bought index exposure.
high-beta-proxies/episode-02.md.takeaway: A daily promise held for a year is not the same promise.

high-beta-proxies/episode-03.md.takeaway: A beta hedge cancels the part of the move the line explained. Everything else is still yours.

chart.title: One earnings day, in dollars
chart.subtitle: The stock falls 15% while the index falls 2%, on a $100,000 long hedged with a $180,000 short.

high-beta-proxies/episode-04.md.key_line: The chain explains the amplification; it does not predict the return.
high-beta-proxies/episode-04.md.takeaway: Walk the chain out loud before you rank anything: a miner is not metal, and a chip supplier is not an index.

high-beta-proxies/episode-05.md.key_line: Beta is a fitted average sensitivity; it is not a worst case.

chart.title: After a 30% index fall, the climb back
chart.subtitle: Beta 1.0 falls about 30%; beta 3.0 falls about 90%. The recovery required is not proportional.

data.note: gain required to return to even, as stated in the text

high-beta-proxies/episode-06.md.key_line: The number is an output of composition, not a property of the plan.
high-beta-proxies/episode-06.md.takeaway: Track weight times beta by sector, not only the total. The ticker count is not the diversification.

market-checklist/episode-01.md.key_line: The label changes what you are allowed to do, not what you predict.

market-checklist/episode-02.md.key_line: First place in a ranking means "look at this next." It never means "buy this."
market-checklist/episode-02.md.takeaway: The screen buys you time to verify. It does not do the verifying.

market-checklist/episode-03.md.key_line: The chart level that invalidates your thesis and the broker order you use to leave are two separate decisions.

market-checklist/episode-04.md.key_line: You take the smallest one. Not the one you like — the smallest.

chart.title: The binding ceiling is the smallest one
chart.subtitle: What each rule permitted for the same trade, and which number survived.

data.note: share of the account, as computed in the text

market-checklist/episode-05.md.key_line: A mental stop is not a stop; it is an intention, and intentions lose to hope in real time.

market-checklist/episode-06.md.key_line: Write the order card before the trigger happens, not while it is happening.

market-checklist/episode-07.md.key_line: Profit can conceal a rule violation, and a loss can come from a correctly executed process.
market-checklist/episode-07.md.takeaway: The review produces one behavior to test, not a verdict on one trade.

market-evidence/episode-01.md.key_line: It is knowing which clock a document runs on.

market-evidence/episode-02.md.key_line: Large volume is evidence of activity, not a decoded portfolio.

market-evidence/episode-03.md.key_line: Notice what that figure actually was: a snapshot, published with a lag, of positions held on a settlement date already in the past.

market-evidence/episode-04.md.key_line: When the primary document cannot be found, the honest label is "unverified", and it stays that way in your notes.

market-evidence/episode-05.md.key_line: A screen that shows a raised price target sitting next to last night's earnings has quietly folded a reaction into a forecast.
market-evidence/episode-05.md.takeaway: Order the evidence by when it was fixed, not by when a screen happened to show it.

market-evidence/episode-06.md.key_line: It is arithmetic performed on things that cannot be added.

options-risk/episode-01.md.key_line: Being right on direction and still losing everything is ordinary here.
options-risk/episode-01.md.takeaway: Read the five fields before you read the view: the contract sets the payoff, and no opinion overrides it.

numbered_titles.1: The contract check before the order

options-risk/episode-02.md.key_line: Use the dials to expose what can hurt you, not to manufacture a forecast.

chart.title: What one day costs, as expiry approaches
chart.subtitle: Daily decay on a typical at-the-money option, in dollars per share, from 90 days out to the final week.

options-risk/episode-03.md.key_line: Every one of these trades is a promise about shares, wearing a premium as a disguise.
options-risk/episode-03.md.takeaway: Accept the share outcome first. The premium is what you are paid for accepting it, never a reason to accept it.

options-risk/episode-04.md.key_line: Read the specification, not the strategy name.

options-risk/episode-05.md.key_line: It is the hurdle you paid for, nothing more.

options-risk/episode-06.md.key_line: They go broke on a good strategy sized wrong.
options-risk/episode-06.md.takeaway: The budget is decided before the trade, and its job is to reject the ones that do not fit.

chart.title: The budget decides the contract count
chart.subtitle: A $30,000 account with a 3% cap allows $900 of loss on one idea; one condor risks $750, two risk $1,500.

portfolio-operator/episode-01.md.key_line: Promotion runs on mechanics, never on profit.
portfolio-operator/episode-01.md.takeaway: Day one has no cushion — buy the information about slippage, fills and your own nerves at the smallest size you will ever pay for it.

portfolio-operator/episode-02.md.key_line: Out-of-sample only protects you if you look once.
portfolio-operator/episode-02.md.takeaway: A backtest is a hypothesis about the past. The forward log begins the day the rules stop moving.

portfolio-operator/episode-03.md.key_line: The fraction matters more than the signal.
portfolio-operator/episode-03.md.takeaway: Drawdown measures the road behind you. The fraction you risk, the volatility you size against and the cluster you forget decide the road ahead.

chart.title: Gain required to return to the previous peak
chart.subtitle: The deeper the hole, the steeper the climb out.

portfolio-operator/episode-04.md.key_line: One number must never move: risk per trade as a share of the account.
portfolio-operator/episode-04.md.takeaway: Size climbs on banked money and proven fills. The fraction you risk climbs on nothing.

chart.title: The rung, not the streak, decides size
chart.subtitle: Round teaching numbers: account level against the trade size allowed there.

portfolio-operator/episode-05.md.key_line: Do I want to stop taking new risk, or do I want to escape the risk I already carry?

portfolio-operator/episode-06.md.key_line: Ten trades tells you about luck, not about the method.
portfolio-operator/episode-06.md.takeaway: Stop on evidence you wrote down in advance, and keep the record append-only — the weeks you would rather delete are the ones that teach.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-01.md.key_line: Any feature not written down starts at no and stays at no until someone can point to data coverage, a test and an owner.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-01.md.takeaway: Everything the desk may do fits on one page — and what is not on the page, it may not do.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-02.md.key_line: It is the line where the evidence stops supporting the machine, and where somebody says so out loud before the account says it for you.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-02.md.takeaway: A control names an action and a person. Anything else is a feeling in costume.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-03.md.key_line: Excitement is paid for in plumbing.

chart.title: The funnel that ends dull
chart.subtitle: Symbols surviving each eligibility filter — counts invented to show the shape, not a screen to copy.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-04.md.key_line: An outage became an abstention instead of a fabrication, and that is the entire return on this week's work.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-05.md.key_line: Same evening, same symbol, three objects with three owners — and the accident to prevent is one quietly being promoted into the next.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-06.md.key_line: Missing is not a value, and the two must never share a cell.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-06.md.takeaway: Stale, missing and zero are three different words because they demand three different answers.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-07.md.key_line: If your program is carrying last month's list of what the service can do, it will happily call something that no longer exists, and it will find that out halfway through a run.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-08.md.key_line: A file downloaded at seven this morning can easily describe the world as it stood two sessions ago, and the download will look perfectly healthy while it does.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-08.md.takeaway: Name the session you meant to trade, and make the file prove it got there.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-09.md.key_line: Two halves from two snapshots are not one answer.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-10.md.key_line: Build your records around the name and your history quietly becomes a mixture of strangers.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-10.md.takeaway: A resolver that guesses is worse than one that refuses.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-11.md.key_line: Squash them and your backtest starts reading tomorrow's newspaper, which is the single most flattering bug in this whole craft.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-12.md.key_line: A price chart can run smooth and straight while the thing underneath it quietly changed shape.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-12.md.takeaway: Freeze the instrument, read the broker's own records, then repair — in that order.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-13.md.key_line: Every page of prices, every filing, every number you compute from them carries that same identifier, or it does not belong to the decision.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-13.md.takeaway: A plan assembled from two moments was never true at either of them.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-14.md.key_line: It says nothing about whether the files are complete, whether the numbers in them are true, or when they were really created.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-15.md.key_line: A replay has to be offline: it reads the frozen bundle, touches no network, changes nothing outside itself, and gives the same answer at three in the morning as at noon.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-15.md.takeaway: The frozen bundle is what lets you debug one thing at a time.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-16.md.key_line: Cheap checks run on everything, and only the survivors earn the slow work of reading a filing or checking an earnings date.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-16.md.takeaway: Cheap first, slow later: research is spent only where it can still change an answer.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-17.md.key_line: So the empty list has to arrive with proof that the machine actually ran, and the proof is a column of counters.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-17.md.takeaway: An empty screen and a broken feed must never print the same sentence.

chart.title: Two counter columns, one empty result
chart.subtitle: Teaching numbers, invented for the lesson: only the counters tell a quiet tape from a feed that never loaded.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-18.md.key_line: Publish the gate that killed the name instead, and readers learn your rules by reading your refusals.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-18.md.takeaway: A refusal a reader can check is worth more than a score they can only obey.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-19.md.key_line: Three indicators computed from the same closing prices are one piece of evidence wearing three hats.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-19.md.takeaway: Evidence drawn from the same prices is one witness repeating itself.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-20.md.key_line: A peer can agree with you; it cannot be your reason.

chart.title: The rally moves the raw number, not the residual
chart.subtitle: Invented figures for the drill: the same pair, before and during a fake market-wide rally.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-21.md.key_line: It becomes one when you write down what has to happen before anything is sent, what would prove the idea wrong, and the date after which the whole thing is dead.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-21.md.takeaway: An entry that cannot expire is an order waiting for bad news to fill it.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-22.md.key_line: Every edit raises the version and records the date it takes effect.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-23.md.key_line: Rebuilding it from what your broker shows is guesswork.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-23.md.takeaway: Holdings tell you what you own, never why you own it.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-24.md.key_line: Partial arming is how a desk ends up holding something nobody decided to hold.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-24.md.takeaway: Execution finishes nothing. Either the plan is complete before it is armed, or it is refused as a block.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-25.md.key_line: Freeze the inputs before the experiment starts, not after you like the answer.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-26.md.key_line: Those 15 are a real position: they need protection, they need to show up when you reconcile, and the missing 25 need a decision rather than silence.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-27.md.key_line: If the conclusion dies with three trades removed, the conclusion was three trades.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-27.md.takeaway: The best of many attempts looks good partly through luck. Say so in the first paragraph, not a footnote.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-28.md.key_line: Which means you compute the quantity several times, once per ceiling, and keep the smallest.

chart.title: Four ceilings, and the sheet keeps the smallest
chart.subtitle: The same name sized four ways on a paper book of 100,000 units. Liquidity governs, not risk.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-29.md.key_line: Both wander over time, so treat them as the input to a limit, never as proof of diversification.

chart.title: Adding the stops, then shocking the bucket
chart.subtitle: One bucket of the book, shocked by three standard deviations, against the loss projected by adding the individual stops.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-30.md.key_line: Those belong in the plan before an order exists, not in your judgement at the moment of placing it.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-30.md.takeaway: A kill state you can talk yourself out of is not a kill state.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-31.md.key_line: Fills at the price you wanted, always, is a bug pretending to be a result.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-31.md.takeaway: A simulator earns its keep by refusing what the broker would refuse, not by filling what you hoped.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-32.md.key_line: Cancel requested may still reach filled — that arrow is legal and it is the one that hurts.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-33.md.key_line: The client has to sit in `unknown`, send nothing, and move only when the broker's own evidence arrives.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-33.md.takeaway: A retry is not free. Until the broker's own history answers, unknown is the only honest state.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-34.md.key_line: Do that once and the ledger stops being evidence; it becomes an opinion you keep updating.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-34.md.takeaway: The chain is arithmetic. The copy you cannot quietly revise is what turns it into evidence.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-35.md.key_line: Half a swap is the dangerous state: you inherit the old exit level and the new position size, a combination nobody designed and nobody reviewed.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-35.md.takeaway: A restart is not a fresh start. It is a claim about which revision was in charge, and whether every open position is still protected.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-36.md.key_line: No envelope is an incident, and it should wake you as loudly as a stack trace would.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-37.md.key_line: A local imitation exists only while your process is alive, and that difference surfaces on exactly the day your process is not.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-38.md.key_line: A code you compute at home proves nothing about an order you never saw acknowledged.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-39.md.key_line: Reconciliation is the habit of keeping those two truths apart.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-39.md.takeaway: The broker holds the shares, so the broker owns the fill. Your plan owns the intent. Everything else is a difference with a name and exactly one permitted repair.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-40.md.key_line: The first screen, meaning the part visible before any scrolling, has to answer that on its own.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-41.md.key_line: On a screen, silence and calm look identical, and only one of the two is safe to act on.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-41.md.takeaway: Unavailable is not a state of calm. It is a fault with an owner, a clock running on it, and a named next step.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-42.md.key_line: People mute what cries wolf, they mute it permanently, and the one message that mattered goes down with the rest.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-43.md.key_line: It is a poor calculator and a worse database, and the trouble is that it never announces which of the three you just asked it to be.
retail-systematic-desk/episode-43.md.takeaway: Let the model argue with you. Never let it count for you.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-44.md.key_line: The gaps you cannot see are the gaps a second pair of eyes was hired to find, and a reviewer who thinks like you has the same blind spots in the same places.

retail-systematic-desk/episode-45.md.key_line: Deciding what counts as success after seeing the numbers is how every desk fools itself.

trade-signal-check/episode-01.md.key_line:
Risking half a percent is
not investing half a percent, and confusing the two is how a position people describe as small ends up
being the largest line they own.
trade-signal-check/episode-01.md.takeaway: Choose the exit first and let the distance decide the quantity. Sliding the stop toward the entry to afford more shares is shopping for a position, not managing risk.

chart.title: One order, two very different percentages
chart.subtitle: Share of a $10,000 account: cash tied up versus the loss planned at the stop.

data.note: The same 51-share order, measured two ways.

trade-signal-check/episode-02.md.key_line:
A distant target is only an unvalidated
scenario until that evidence exists.

numbered_titles.0: Four items behind a headline ratio

trade-signal-check/episode-03.md.key_line: A number without a method is only a loss budget.
trade-signal-check/episode-03.md.takeaway: ATR measures how much the stock has been moving. Only the setup's own record of adverse moves says where the protective exit belongs.

trade-signal-check/episode-04.md.key_line:
A
stop placed inside that empty interval could not create a buyer at its chosen level.
trade-signal-check/episode-04.md.takeaway: A stop instructs an order; it does not reserve a price. Decide the earnings treatment while the position is still hypothetical.

trade-signal-check/episode-05.md.key_line: Precision without reproducible provenance is only decoration, not decision-grade evidence.
trade-signal-check/episode-05.md.takeaway: A number can be exact and still prove nothing. Direction, ownership and coverage have to come from the file itself, not from the label above the dashboard.

trade-signal-check/episode-06.md.key_line: At execution time, any hard failure stops the trade.

trading-journal-feedback-loop/episode-01.key_line: Of all the columns, the uncomfortable one is "plan followed, yes or no".
